is the largest positive integer dividing both nonzero integers; equivalently it is the positive generator of all integer combinations ax+by.
Repeated Euclidean division finds the gcd; reversing the divisions finds Bézout coefficients. In particular, a and b are coprime exactly when some integer combination of them equals 1.

items.text: Divisibility is an integer statement; division in the rational or real numbers is not the same relation.
Any common divisor divides every integer combination ax+by.
The coefficients in Bézout's identity are generally not unique.
This handbook uses gcd(a,0)=|a| and gcd(0,0)=0.

items.text: Do not confuse gcd(a,b)=1 with a and b both being prime.
Keep the remainder nonnegative and strictly smaller than the divisor's absolute value.
The product formula for lcm needs the absolute value when signed integers are allowed.
